one_line: Meitei king of Manipur who, allied with the British, led the Gambhir Singh Levy to liberate his kingdom from Burmese rule during the First Anglo-Burmese War.

appearance.age_look: mid-30s, athletic and wiry, with the lean build of a campaign-hardened cavalry commander
appearance.face: oval face with high cheekbones, warm medium-brown complexion, straight nose, neatly trimmed moustache with a short pointed goatee, sharp dark-brown eyes under slightly arched brows, default expression calm and determined with a hint of fierce focus
appearance.hair: black hair tied in a tight topknot at the back of the crown, sides smoothly combed back; front hairline clean with no loose fringe; a narrow white cotton headband wraps around the forehead, and a simple small gold tilak-like mark sits just above the brow center
appearance.costume: He wears an early-19th-century Meitei royal-military outfit: a long, fitted white cotton jama-style tunic reaching mid-thigh, closing left-over-right with cloth ties and a subtle narrow red piping along the front opening and cuffs; over this is a sleeveless, hip-length deep-red cotton angarkha-style overcoat with a slightly flared skirt, plain but for a thin gold border at the edges. Around his waist is a wide, tightly wrapped dark-indigo cotton sash (pacheng-like) knotted on his left side, with one short end hanging to mid-thigh. His lower garment is a white cotton dhoti wrapped firmly and brought between the legs for riding, with a modest border of thin red and gold stripes along the edge; it falls to the ankles but is neatly hitched to allow movement, never exposing the thighs. He wears simple brown leather riding boots reaching mid-calf, slightly worn and strapped, historically plausible for a mounted commander in Company-allied service. A narrow, embroidered off-white shawl with a red and gold woven border is draped over his left shoulder and across the chest, tucked lightly into the sash. Jewellery is restrained: a pair of small gold hoop earrings, a thin gold chain with a tiny circular pendant under the tunic neckline, and a plain gold armlet on his right upper arm visible where the overcoat armhole is wide. The fabrics are matte cotton and light wool, with subtle handloom texture and no flashy patterns beyond the narrow borders.
appearance.signature: A single slightly curved Meitei-style sword (a war dao) with a broad blade and no handguard, carried sheathed at his left hip in a plain dark-brown leather scabbard with a brass mouthpiece, the hilt wrapped in dark-red cord with a simple brass pommel; in dramatic poses he grips it one-handed, blade angled forward, embodying his leadership of the Gambhir Singh Levy.

ref_desc: Raja Gambhir Singh is a mid-30s Meitei king with an oval medium-brown face, black hair in a topknot with a white headband, wearing a white jama, deep-red sleeveless overcoat, indigo sash, white dhoti and brown boots, carrying a curved Meitei sword in a dark-brown scabbard with red-wrapped hilt and gold details.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of Raja Gambhir Singh from Manipur, showing him front and back and a close-up of his face: a mid-30s, athletic Meitei king with an oval medium-brown face, high cheekbones, sharp dark-brown eyes, a neatly trimmed moustache and short pointed goatee, and black hair tied in a tight topknot with a white cotton headband and a small gold mark above the brow. Dress him in an early-19th-century Meitei royal-military outfit: a fitted white cotton jama-style tunic to mid-thigh with subtle red piping along the opening and cuffs, over which he wears a sleeveless deep-red cotton overcoat with a thin gold border, a wide dark-indigo cotton sash wrapped firmly at the waist and knotted on his left, and a white cotton dhoti with thin red and gold border edges wrapped to the ankles and arranged for riding, always modestly covering the legs. Give him plain brown leather mid-calf riding boots with straps, an off-white shawl with red and gold border draped from his left shoulder and tucked into the sash, small gold hoop earrings, a thin gold chain at the neck, and a simple gold armlet on his right upper arm. His signature weapon is a slightly curved Meitei sword in a dark-brown leather scabbard with a brass mouthpiece, the hilt wrapped in dark-red cord with a simple brass pommel, hanging from his left hip and also shown unsheathed in one pose. Use a palette of white, deep red, dark indigo, brown leather and gold, keeping fabrics matte and historically plausible, and emphasize a calm yet fierce commander’s expression suitable for a leader allied with British forces to liberate Manipur.
